LanguageData.HE_Inti_BS_TerraceFarmer.title: terrace farmer
LanguageData.HE_Inti_BS_TerraceFarmer.description: [PAWN_nameDef] farmed a staircase of fields on a mountainside, potatoes at the top, maize at the bottom and quinoa in between. [PAWN_pronoun] can rebuild a fallen terrace wall in a day.
LanguageData.HE_Inti_BS_Khipukamayuq.title: khipukamayuq
LanguageData.HE_Inti_BS_Khipukamayuq.description: [PAWN_nameDef] kept the quipus of a whole province: every llama, every sack of maize and every soldier, tied in coloured knots. [PAWN_pronoun] can still read a cord by touch in the dark.
LanguageData.HE_Inti_BS_Stonemason.title: imperial stonemason
LanguageData.HE_Inti_BS_Stonemason.description: [PAWN_nameDef] shaped blocks so precisely that they fit without mortar, pounding granite with harder stones until the joints vanished.
LanguageData.HE_Inti_BS_Chaski.title: chaski runner
LanguageData.HE_Inti_BS_Chaski.description: [PAWN_nameDef] ran [PAWN_possessive] stretch of the great road day and night, a quipu in [PAWN_possessive] bag and a conch at [PAWN_possessive] lips. [PAWN_pronoun] has never been the one who made a message late.
LanguageData.HE_Inti_BS_Slinger.title: army slinger
LanguageData.HE_Inti_BS_Slinger.description: [PAWN_nameDef] marched in the front ranks of the imperial army, sling in hand and a bag of stones at the hip. [PAWN_pronoun] can split a gourd at fifty paces.
LanguageData.HE_Inti_BS_Herbalist.title: kallawaya healer
LanguageData.HE_Inti_BS_Herbalist.description: [PAWN_nameDef] walked from the cloud forests to the high plains with a bag of herbs, setting bones and treating fevers in every village on the way.
LanguageData.HE_Inti_BS_Weaver.title: aqlla weaver
LanguageData.HE_Inti_BS_Weaver.description: [PAWN_nameDef] wove the fine cloth of the court, so tight it held water, with tocapu patterns that only a few could read.
LanguageData.HE_Inti_BS_Trader.title: llama caravan trader
LanguageData.HE_Inti_BS_Trader.description: [PAWN_nameDef] led strings of llamas from the coast to the mountains, trading dried fish and salt for wool and potatoes, and talked [PAWN_possessive] way out of every ambush.
LanguageData.HE_Inti_BS_LlamaChild.title: llama herder
LanguageData.HE_Inti_BS_LlamaChild.description: [PAWN_nameDef] herded llamas and alpacas on the high grasslands, a sling in one hand to chase off foxes.
LanguageData.HE_Inti_BS_TerraceChild.title: terrace child
LanguageData.HE_Inti_BS_TerraceChild.description: [PAWN_nameDef] carried baskets of soil up the terrace stairs and planted seed potatoes before [PAWN_pronoun] could count.
LanguageData.HE_Inti_BS_KnotPupil.title: knot school pupil
LanguageData.HE_Inti_BS_KnotPupil.description: [PAWN_nameDef] was chosen for the school of the knot keepers and spent years tying and untying counts under a strict teacher.
LanguageData.HE_Inti_BS_FisherChild.title: lake fisher's child
LanguageData.HE_Inti_BS_FisherChild.description: [PAWN_nameDef] grew up on a reed island in a cold high lake, fishing from a reed boat and patching it every evening.
